userAcquisition:
Our first users are Python developers building research assistants, internal knowledge tools and content publishing workflows. Their first task is concrete: move a signed research note from one application to another, detect changed bytes and read issuer revocation without relying on the originating platform API.

The current entry points are an MIT Python SDK/CLI, a public repository with reproducible Chinese and English setup instructions, and two live testnet applications. A public synthetic receipt lets developers try independent verification without installing a wallet or sharing private content. The two-application example then shows how to integrate issuance and consumption in their own workflow.

Initial acquisition is developer-led: share the open-source walkthrough and short working-product demo with relevant Python/AI builder communities and Monad ecosystem developers, then invite a small number of interested builders to complete the integration task. Outreach will be performed by the entrant or with explicit authorization; no outreach or adoption is claimed to have happened.

The first milestone is one real external developer completing the end-to-end integration. Record time to first valid verification, setup failures, cross-application portability and revocation handling, alongside qualitative feedback and willingness to use the toolkit. Improve the SDK and error states from those observations before expanding distribution. We do not claim existing users, revenue, market size or a measured success rate. Future hosted verification/indexing options would be evaluated only after evidence of repeated integration demand.
judgeAccess:
No login or wallet is required to verify the public sample.

1. Open https://prooftrail-consumer.vercel.app and click 载入真实链上样例 (Load live-chain example). This loads public synthetic content and its portable JSON; it does not pre-approve the result.
2. Click 检查并生成预览 (Check and preview). The independent Python consumer reads Monad Testnet chain 10143 and the trusted registry, displaying all verification checks and a private preview.
3. Edit the original text and check again. Content integrity fails and preview is refused. Load the sample again to restore the original bytes.
4. For revoked evidence, use artifacts/monad-demo/revoked-content.txt and revoked-receipt.json from the public repository https://github.com/linlin449/ProofTrail. Paste the exact UTF-8 content and JSON into the consumer; live revocation should prevent preview.
5. To issue your own receipt, open https://prooftrail-issuer.vercel.app in an EVM-wallet browser, select Monad Testnet (10143) and use a dedicated account with test MON. Complete the typed-data signature and registration transaction in your wallet. The server holds no issuer key. Browser-wallet end-to-end review remains pending.

Registry: 0xd4c01FEdb19eF081AAF3c6814316d8CeF7579Cd7. Source verification is an exact creation/runtime match on Sourcify. Source, Chinese instructions, raw transaction evidence and independent CLI examples are in the public repository.

Public Hobby hosting may have cold starts; a network failure never produces a valid result. Online verification sees the submitted text; use only public synthetic content for review. Provenance is not factual truth, copyright or real-world identity. The current technical screenshot video is a review aid, not the final working-product recording.
